quickAnswer: A rigorous weighted evaluation rubric snow and storm cleanup contingency clauses grades janitorial bidders across 100 points: Missed-Visit Credit & Hour-Banking Transparency (30 points), Emergency Storm Response SLA & Geolocation Verification (25 points), Pre-Locked Specialty Extraction Pricing at $55–$95/hr (20 points), Winter Salt Neutralization & Walk-Off Matting Scope (15 points), and COI / OSHA Wet-Hazard Compliance (10 points). blocks.text: Why Verbal Promises About Storm Readiness Fail During Regional Emergencies

During a janitorial sales presentation for a 10,000 to 24,999 square foot office ($0.07 to $0.12 per square foot per visit) or a 2,500 to 9,999 square foot facility ($0.09 to $0.15 per square foot), every account executive promises that their company is 'on call 24/7 for snow, storm, and water emergencies' and 'always fair about snow-day credits.' Yet when a regional nor'easter, ice storm, or flash flood hits thirty buildings in the contractor's portfolio on the same night, verbal assurances evaporate. Unprepared contractors prioritize their largest hospital or stadium accounts, leave your lobby salt-crusted for a week, and bill your full 21.65-visit monthly retainer (5x/week based on 4.33 weeks/month at the 0.90 frequency multiplier).

Applying a weighted evaluation rubric snow and storm cleanup contingency clauses during the RFP phase forces bidders to substantiate their weather protocols with binding contract language, pre-priced specialty labor tables ($55 to $95/hour), and verified local equipment reserves.
The 100-Point Snow & Storm Contingency Procurement Scorecard

Distribute this 100-point scoring matrix to your procurement committee when evaluating finalist proposals. Score each vendor solely on written clauses included in their draft Master Services Agreement (MSA) and verified warehouse inventory—never on verbal Q&A answers.

blocks.caption: 100-Point Weighted Evaluation Rubric for Snow and Storm Cleanup Contingency Clauses
rows: 1. Missed-Visit Credit & Hour-Bank Mechanism
30 Points
Flat monthly fee with no credit or hour rollover during weather closures
Informal promise to 'make up work on next visit' without hour accounting (15 pts)
Client choice of 100% pro-rata credit (Fee / 21.65) or 1:1 banked deep-floor hours valid 60 days (30 pts)
2. Emergency Response SLA & Local Reserve Fleet
25 Points
No guaranteed response window; wet extractors shared from out-of-state warehouse
8-to-12 hour best-effort response; limited portable wet-dry shop vacuums (13 pts)
Guaranteed 2-to-4 hr on-site SLA within 25-mile radius; dedicated wet extractors & air movers (25 pts)
3. Pre-Locked Specialty & Overtime Rate Table
20 Points
Emergency storm or flood cleanup 'quoted per event' or billed > $135/hr
Fixed overtime multiplier (1.5x standard $35-$65/hr rate) but equipment rental uncapped (10 pts)
Pre-locked $55-$95/hr specialty extraction rate inclusive of wet-vac machinery; draws banked hours first (20 pts)
4. Winter Salt Neutralization & Matting Protocol
15 Points
Plain water mopping on VCT (1.04x) / Tile (1.12x); no winter mat extraction schedule
Neutral cleaner used daily, but acid salt-rinse and mat extraction billed as extra T&M (8 pts)
Acidic salt-neutralizer rinse & nightly entrance mat vacuuming/extraction bundled Nov-Apr at $0 extra (15 pts)
5. Geofenced Attendance, OSHA & COI Compliance
10 Points
Paper sign-in sheets; no clear boundary between indoor janitorial and exterior snow liability
Supervisor phone check-in during storms; basic General Liability COI (5 pts)
GPS/badge timeclock verification, ANSI wet-floor signage staging, full COI & Workers' Comp audit (10 pts)

blocks.text: Four Verification Audits to Validate Contractor Storm Claims

A bidder can easily type '2-hour emergency storm response' into a proposal template. Before awarding the full 25 points in Category 2 or 15 points in Category 4, run these four operational verification checks:

items.name: Audit the Ratio of Local Wet Extractors to Active Client Accounts
items.text: Ask the bidder how many commercial wet extractors, flood pump-out units, and high-CFM carpet air movers they warehouse within 25 miles of your building, and divide that number by their active local accounts. If a vendor serves 45 offices with only 2 wet extractors, they cannot deliver simultaneous storm recovery.

items.name: Test the Monthly Invoice Math for Pro-Rata Transparency
items.text: Verify that the contract pricing page shows the exact per-visit calculation across 4.33 weeks/month (1.0 visit/mo for monthly, 2.17 for biweekly, 4.33 for 1x/week, 8.66 for 2x/week, 13.0 for 3x/week, 21.65 for 5x/week, or 30.33 for 7x/week) and explicitly notes whether the $90 to $135 minimum visit fee applies to small offices under 2,500 sq ft.

items.name: Verify Winter Chemical SDS Sheets and Floor Finish Guarantees
items.text: Request the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for the contractor's winter ice-melt neutralizer. Confirm it is formulated to dissolve calcium and magnesium chloride deposits on VCT (1.04x multiplier), ceramic tile (1.12x), and polished concrete (0.95x) without stripping floor sealer.

items.name: Inspect the Certificate of Insurance (COI) for Water & Slip-and-Fall Scope
items.text: Confirm the contractor carries at least $1,000,000 per occurrence / $2,000,000 aggregate Commercial General Liability coverage without exclusions for interior water-extraction operations, plus active Workers' Compensation covering late-night storm dispatches.

blocks.title: How to Score Banked Hours Against Your Quarterly Deep Floor Program
blocks.text: If your facility already purchases the Quarterly Deep Floor Care add-on ($0.03 to $0.06 per sq ft per month amortized), award full rubric points only to vendors who allow unused weather-closure hours to fund additional mid-winter lobby carpet extraction or spring VCT scrub-and-recoat passes—never duplicate work already paid for in your quarterly schedule.
Hardening Facility Restrooms and Entrances Against Storm-Related Supply Disruptions

Scoring a vendor's storm contingency goes hand-in-hand with auditing your building's dispenser resilience. When blizzards or severe storms delay delivery trucks or compress night cleaning windows, small-capacity paper and sanitizer dispensers run dry by mid-afternoon, driving tenant complaints even when your janitorial contract is well structured. Upgrading to high-capacity, low-touch commercial hardware protects service continuity across restrooms ($15 to $30 per visit) and breakrooms ($12 to $25 per visit).

In office breakrooms and single-occupant restrooms, installing the Georgia-Pacific enMotion Impulse 8-Inch Compact Towel Dispenser provides an 8-in Roll capacity in a Compact Depth wall footprint with hygienic Touchless dispensing powered by a long-lasting 4 D-Cell battery bank. Inside multi-stall restrooms, mounting the Georgia-Pacific Compact Vertical Coreless Toilet Paper Dispenser doubles reserve capacity with a 2x Coreless configuration holding up to 3000 Sheets in an ADA Slim housing secured by a Keyed Lock, preventing tissue runouts when a storm forces a 24-hour shift postponement. At building entrances and elevator lobbies where wet commuters congregate, staging the GOJO PURELL ES8 Touch-Free Hand Sanitizer Dispenser offers a 1200 mL cartridge with Energy-on-Refill battery replacement, ADA Compliant depth, and At-a-Glance level monitoring so porters can verify stock levels in seconds.
Comparing Two Finalist Bidders Using the Storm Contingency Rubric

Consider how this weighted evaluation rubric breaks a tie between two bidders on a 25,000-square-foot regional headquarters (in the 25,000+ sq ft bracket of $0.05 to $0.10 per sq ft per visit) cleaned 5x/week (21.65 visits/month at the 0.90 frequency multiplier):

items: Vendor Alpha quotes $0.068/sq ft/visit ($36,805/yr) and scores 48/100 on the storm rubric: no pro-rata credit for closures, unpriced emergency flood extraction ('market rates apply'), and plain-water mopping on lobby tile.

Vendor Beta quotes $0.072/sq ft/visit ($38,970/yr) and scores 94/100: full pro-rata credit or 60-day hour banking, guaranteed 3-hour water extraction SLA at $68/hr specialty labor (inside the $55 to $95/hr benchmark), and free winter ice-melt neutralizer from November through April.

Financial Verdict: Two winter storm closures (worth $3,240 in credited or banked labor) plus a single avoided spring VCT strip-and-wax repair ($2,200) make Vendor Beta more than $3,200 cheaper per year in true total cost of occupancy.

faqs.q: What score on the 100-point snow and storm contingency rubric should be required for northern or coastal offices?
faqs.a: Facilities in snow-belt states (Northeast, Midwest, Mountain West) or Gulf/Atlantic hurricane zones should require a minimum score of 85/100, with full credit (30/30 points) in Category 1 (Missed-Visit Credits & Hour Banking) and at least 20/25 points in Category 2 (2-to-4 Hour Emergency Response SLA with local wet extraction inventory).

faqs.q: How do we verify that banked snow-day hours were actually worked later in the quarter?
faqs.a: Require the contractor to maintain a shared 'Inclement Weather Hour Ledger' attached to the monthly invoice. Whenever a closure adds hours to the bank (calculated using your contracted nightly hours or the 3,500 sq ft/hr ISSA production rate), and whenever a post-storm deep floor shift draws hours down, the ledger must list the date, technician badge swipe timestamps, and specific task completed (e.g., 6 hours lobby carpet salt extraction).

faqs.q: Should emergency storm cleanup rates apply during regular weekday shift hours?
faqs.a: No. If a storm cleanup or salt-extraction task is performed during the crew's normal scheduled evening shift using regular staff, it should be covered by standard hourly rates ($35 to $65/hour) or drawn from banked closure hours. Pre-locked specialty rates ($55 to $95/hour) should only apply to unscheduled emergency call-outs, weekend flood responses, or heavy restoration equipment deployments beyond the daily scope.

faqs.q: How does our lease structure affect who scores and enforces storm cleanup clauses?
faqs.a: In a Full-Service Gross lease where the landlord contracts building-wide janitorial services, tenants should request the property manager's winter lobby matting and storm credit policy during lease operating-expense (CAM) audits. In a Triple-Net (NNN) or single-tenant facility where you contract the janitorial vendor directly, your facility team controls 100% of the contingency rubric and invoice credits.
